tasks.title: Reorganize Coder Session into a structured execution-evidence view
tasks.description: Formalize the existing Coder Session shell into stable regions for task identity and status, usage, errors, transcript turns and tool calls, follow-up actions, and sibling evidence. Add the read-only errors summary and workflow-context navigation while preserving existing transcript, cancel, recovery, follow-up, sibling, and lineage behavior, and migrate all session status surfaces to the shared theme-token families.
acceptanceCriteria: SessionDetailShell renders recognizable, stable regions for task identity/current status, optional usage, optional errors, transcript turns and tool calls, follow-up actions, and optional sibling sessions; sessions without usage, errors, turns, or siblings degrade without moving or merging the remaining regions.

A compact session-errors-region appears above the transcript when failureReason, failureCategory, or toolErrorCount indicates an error, exposes data-failure-category and data-tool-error-count for verification, and is absent when no error evidence exists.

The existing transcript hierarchy continues to distinguish tool calls from message turns, and the transcript scroll container, sticky title, sticky recovery bar, follow-up composer, sibling navigation slot, lineage link, and cancel confirmation anchors and behavior remain available with their existing gating semantics.

Issue-bound sessions expose project-scoped entry points to the relevant issue and workflow context; sibling and lineage links remain project-scoped; generic sessions without an issue link to their agent context and do not fabricate issue or workflow links.

Status badges for running, completed, failed, stale, probing, and finalizing sessions, plus failure, recovery, context-health, usage, follow-up, and sibling status accents, use the shared success/warning/info/danger and neutral surface token families in light and dark mode; no parallel shared status helper or hardcoded semantic red/amber/yellow/blue/green palette remains on these session surfaces.

The implementation consumes the existing session metadata, transcript, usage, sibling, and lineage data sources without API, DTO, query, transcript-recording, subscription, or action-semantics changes and without exposing raw implementation field names as labels.

Existing SessionPage sticky, cancel, lineage, header, follow-up, and GenericSessionPage tests are updated and pass; focused spec coverage verifies region order and optional-region degradation, error presence/absence, project-scoped navigation, action preservation, and shared token classes in both themes using existing DI seams and MSW without vi.mock.
npm run typecheck -w packages/web and npm run test:run -w packages/web pass.
tasks.output: Structured Coder Session evidence layout in packages/web/src/pages/session and related coder-session/session-health widgets, with preserved actions and navigation plus updated unit/spec tests
tasks.notes: Covers the complete coder-session-evidence-view capability and design D4-D7. Keep session-recovery-bar inside the transcript scroll container, make session-errors-region read-only, preserve existing test anchors where still valid, and use local inline status-presentation records rather than reintroducing shared/status-presentation.

tasks.title: Replace Activity session cards with an attention-first event evidence feed
tasks.description: Build a pure ActivityEvent projection over the existing activity, generic-session, and runner projections, then replace the Active/Waiting/Recent card sections with event entries carrying production event type, attention level, timestamps, and navigation targets. Deliver the collapsible attention and routine zones, event/attention filters, generic-session coverage, direct evidence links, and shared theme-token treatment as one usable Activity module.
acceptanceCriteria: A pure buildActivityEvents projection and composing hook produce ActivityEvent entries with type, attention, time, domain-language title/description, and project-scoped targets from existing snapshots; entries distinguish issue-state, workflow-stage, agent-session, runner, and failure evidence without claiming reconstruction of unavailable transition history.

Failed sessions produce a failure entry with failure attention and retain a separate routine agent-session lifecycle entry; waiting approval and blocked evidence receive approval/blocked attention; busy or stale runners produce runner entries while idle runners remain summarized; all entries have deterministic ordering and duplicate session IDs are merged only once.

Generic agent-launched and workflow-bound sessions appear together with the same agent-session event identity; workflow sessions link directly to their issue-scoped session route, generic sessions link directly to /agent-sessions/:sessionId, and generic sessions are not excluded or duplicated because they lack a workflow binding.

ActivityPage renders activity-attention-zone before activity-routine-zone whenever failure, approval, or blocked entries exist, omits the attention zone entirely when none exist, and orders entries most-recent-first within their attention/type grouping so routine evidence never precedes needs-attention evidence on the first screen.

The activity-filter-bar can isolate each supported event type and attention-only evidence and can clear filters to restore the complete attention-ordered feed; every activity-event-entry exposes data-event-type and data-attention identities.

Every applicable entry provides the most specific project-scoped primary destination plus available issue, workflow-context, session, agent, or runner secondary targets; activity-runners-link remains available and no context-less root route is introduced.

Activity event entries, attention markers, filters, StatusBar/runner/session status surfaces, and issue-event-timeline category and marker styles use shared success/warning/info/danger and neutral surface token families in light and dark mode; hardcoded semantic red/amber/orange/yellow/blue/green/gray palette classes covered by design D5 are removed without adding a shared status-presentation module.

The feature uses only existing activity, session, issue/workflow snapshot, and runner projections and endpoints; it adds no server, runner, CLI, API/DTO, event-recording, event-emission, transcript-recording, or event/session-subscription behavior and exposes only production/domain labels.

Collocated activity-events unit tests cover all classification and ordering rules, failure dual entries, generic-session merging/deduplication, and target construction; ActivityPage and new evidence-view spec tests cover event identity, attention-zone presence/absence and prominence, filtering/clearing, direct navigation, and light/dark token classes using MSW/DI seams and fake timers without vi.mock or wall-clock waits.
npm run typecheck -w packages/web and npm run test:run -w packages/web pass.
tasks.output: ActivityEvent projection and attention-first ActivityPage feed in packages/web/src/pages/activity and related activity/session/timeline/runner widgets, with complete unit/spec coverage
tasks.notes: Covers the complete activity-evidence-view capability and design D1-D3 plus D5-D7. Do not reuse EventTimelinePanel or add a cross-issue event stream. Derive snapshot evidence from existing data, preserve activity-runners-link, route all links through useProjectPath(), control Activity timers in tests, and keep filter-chip logic local rather than extracting a speculative shared component. Dependency analysis: T-002 does not consume T-001 output, so no dependency edge is required.
